name: Central City and the Octagon
tagline: Victorian stone facades around an eight-sided civic square
description: Dunedin's compact core radiates from the Octagon, ringed by the town hall, art gallery, theatres and a tight run of bars and restaurants. Warehouse Precinct conversions to the south hold studios, roasteries and small offices. Everything in the flat central grid is within a ten minute walk.
bestFor: Nomads who want to live car free with cafes, coworking and the library on their doorstep.
pros: Flat, compact and fully walkable core
Best cafes, coworking and coffee roasters in the city
Heritage stone architecture and a real civic centre
cons: Bar noise around the Octagon on weekend nights
Older apartments are cold and poorly insulated
Very quiet on Sundays, much closes early

name: North Dunedin
tagline: Student flats packed around the University of Otago
description: The dense grid of timber villas between the Otago campus and the botanic garden, home to most of the university's students. Rents per room are the lowest in the city, the Leith runs through it, and cheap eateries and bike shops line Castle and Albany streets. Term time is loud and social.
bestFor: Budget travellers and younger nomads who want the cheapest rent and an instant social scene.
pros: Cheapest rooms and flats in Dunedin
Walk to campus, botanic garden and the centre
Constant events, cheap food and easy people-meeting
cons: Notoriously cold, damp flats with poor heating
Loud parties through the university term
Almost empty and dull over the summer break

name: St Clair
tagline: Surf beach, esplanade cafes and a heated saltwater pool
description: Dunedin's beachfront suburb on the southern coast, where the esplanade looks out over a consistent surf break and the historic saltwater pool. Cafes along Forbury Road do the city's best brunch. Housing is a mix of villas and newer townhouses, and the crowd skews surfers, families and retirees.
bestFor: Surfers and outdoor types who want a beach walk before the first meeting of the day.
pros: Surf beach, esplanade and heated pool at the door
cons: Exposed to strong southerly winds and sea spray
About 4km from the centre, most people drive or bus

name: Roslyn
tagline: Hilltop village shops with views over the harbour
description: A settled suburb on the ridge above the city, built around a small shopping strip on Highgate with a supermarket, bakeries, a cinema and good cafes. Streets of well-kept villas look down over the harbour. It is quiet, family-oriented and only a short bus or steep walk from the centre.
bestFor: Long stayers who want quiet, sunlight and harbour views with local shops within walking distance.
pros: Its own shops, supermarket and cafes on the ridge
Sunnier and better views than the valley floor
Quiet family streets, close to the centre
cons: The walk down is easy, the walk back up is steep
Little nightlife beyond a couple of bars
Rents run above the city average

name: Port Chalmers
tagline: Working port township with galleries and an artist crowd
description: A small harbourside town about 13km up the coast, where a working container port sits beside a main street of galleries, a good bakery, cafes and a legendary pub. Artists and musicians have long based here for the cheap old cottages and the wildlife on the peninsula opposite.
bestFor: Quiet-seeking creatives who want cheap character housing and harbour walks over city convenience.
pros: Strong arts community and harbour scenery
Wildlife, walking tracks and the peninsula nearby
cons: A 20 minute drive from the city, and buses are limited
Port and rail noise from the container terminal
Very few services, you shop in the city for most things
